youtube.title: Why Rome Had a 445-Day Year 😵 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description: Ancient Rome's calendar was so far off that harvest festivals fell in the wrong season. So in 46 BC, Julius Caesar, advised by the astronomer Sosigenes of Alexandria, fixed it. To catch up, that one year ran for 445 days, and Romans called it the year of confusion. Then came a simple rule: three years of 365 days, and every fourth year one extra day. The leap year was born. Full episode on the channel. #Shorts #rome #leapyear #history #thehiddenwhy
